key_insight: AEAPTMS amino-silane passivation makes perovskite surface electrostatics more uniform and stable, reducing grain-boundary barriers and improving photovoltage dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This points to a practical surface-passivation strategy for lowering voltage losses and improving stability in perovskite solar cells.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) on mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films
Compare dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV) before vs. after AEAPTMS treatment
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior responses; probe wavelength-dependent SPV for sub-bandgap disorder
evidence_signal: AEAPTMS narrowed dark CPD distribution from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from ~345 to ~417 mV, and reduced the SPV stabilization time constant from ~840 to ~470 s.
watch_item: KPFM surface signals are highly sensitive to film preparation and environmental conditions, so nanoscale trends may not translate directly to full-device performance without further validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
